agree.reason: Showing that the public share ($49,000) is about what the town gave last time ($47,000), and that every pledge comes back if the goal is missed, answers my memory of the refunds well. But nothing speaks to my having just given $200 to the ambulance fund, and nothing suggests what a pledge should be, so I'd likely give something modest rather than stretch.

honest.reason: Every number is accurate, but the document leaves out that the roof estimate is from last fall and could rise by up to 15%, and it says "this town pledged $47,000" when the brief only says the campaign reached that figure.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly works out the $49,000 still needed and sets it against last time's $47,000, which is its strongest move, but it never works out the per-resident share (about $7.50 across 6,500 people), the yearly attendance (about 9,400 tickets), or the daily pace needed between May 1 and June 30.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the alternative accurately (no cinema, with the nearest one 38 miles away) and compares fairly with the earlier campaign, though it doesn't say what happens to the building or the $1 lease if this campaign fails.

qualification.reason: The all-or-nothing condition is clear and checkable ($85,000, June 30, full refund), but the real open risk, a roof cost that could rise by up to 15%, isn't mentioned or backed by a contingency.

objections.reason: It meets the "last time ended in refunds" objection head on, but it doesn't deal with competing local causes like the ambulance fund, or with worries about running costs once the cinema reopens.

fit.reason: It's a clear, well-organized crowdfunding pitch, well under 350 words and signed by the chair.
